description: A second journey through Cornwall moves between fishermen, artists, farmers, folklore and industrial history, with Rick using dishes such as stargazy pie, king crab, razor clams and the Cornish pasty to connect landscape with local identity.

s12e01.description: Rick recalls the improvised beginnings of his first restaurant, swims at Bude Sea Pool and heads off Land's End to learn traditional handlining before cooking a fish pie for Tresillian head gardener John Harris.

s12e02.description: St Ives painter Alfred Wallis, a farm on the Cornwall-Devon border and St Neot's medieval glass lead Rick toward a lamb navarin and the village's eccentric Oak Apple Day procession.

s12e03.description: Biologist Gillian Burke guides Rick through the Atlantic temperate rainforest beside the Helford River; a Cornish charcuterie maker then inspires a high tea built around cured meats, ham and vegetables.

s12e04.description: The Mermaid of Zennor folktale sends Rick along the coast to edible seaweed gatherers before he cooks gurnard with parsley, garlic and sea spaghetti, then watches Redruth stock-car racing and visits a Bodmin Moor blacksmith.

s12e05.description: Artist Sue Read and Mousehole's stories of Dylan Thomas and fisherman Tom Bawcock lead to a proper stargazy pie, before Rick follows Thomas Hardy's little-known Cornish love story along the dramatic north coast.

s12e06.description: Rick heads out from Newquay for sweet spider crab, cooks it with fennel and samphire, then travels inland to Bodmin Moor to see Robin Hanbury-Tenison's rewilding project and the return of beavers.

s12e07.description: On the Isles of Scilly, Rick meets a traditional lobster-pot maker, recounts the disastrous 1707 naval wrecks and visits a project protecting native honeybees before making a steamed pudding with honey-butterscotch sauce.

s12e08.description: At Davidstow, Rick meets a professional cheese grader and makes cheese-and-chive scones, then heads to Newlyn to explore the painters who turned the fishing town into an important art colony.

s12e09.description: Falmouth's former role in imperial communications and its working harbour lead to William Golding's daughter and the wartime experiences behind Lord of the Flies, followed by a chef who cooks almost entirely over wood.

s12e10.description: A professional forager leads Rick around the Camel Estuary through edible and dangerous plants, while fish supplier Matthew Stevens and chef Ed Rowe open a discussion about local food and the pressures of second-home tourism.

s12e11.description: Rick joins divers hunting razor clams and grills them Shangurro-style, then follows Newlyn's role as a navigational datum and visits Penlee Museum to see the copperwork associated with Cornwall's craft tradition.

s12e12.description: J. M. W. Turner's response to the Cornish landscape leads Rick to Newlyn Fish Market's early-morning auction and onward to Caerhays Castle, whose gardens preserve the legacy of Victorian plant hunters.

s12e13.description: Beside the Tamar, Rick investigates Sir James Tillie's macabre mausoleum, tastes chef Emily Scott's G7 turbot dish, visits an asparagus grower and meets the Wave Project, which uses surfing as therapy for young people.

s12e14.description: In Looe, Rick recalls Barbary raids that carried Cornish people into slavery, then joins one of St Mawes' remaining fishing boats, cooks warm sole salad and meets Newlyn chefs making the most of local mackerel and seafood.

s12e15.description: Rick beachcombs the Rame Peninsula, studies a remarkable archive of early Bude photography and visits a mine to trace how the Cornish pasty evolved from upper-class food into practical fuel for miners.
